trade.text: He opposes a trade war with Canada and supports fair trade while confronting unfair practices.
trade.quote: I strongly oppose picking a trade war with Canada, our closest ally and one of Michigan’s most important economic partners.

housing.text: He said Congress should encourage more housing construction and limit corporate purchases of residential properties.
housing.quote: Congress should encourage the construction of more housing while limiting corporations from buying up residential properties.

immigration.text: He supports modernizing legal immigration pathways, protecting due process, and focusing enforcement on actual threats.
immigration.quote: We should reduce processing backlogs, modernize legal immigration pathways, and ensure decisions are made efficiently and fairly.

guns.text: He said he would break with Democrats to protect the Second Amendment and law-abiding citizens’ right to own firearms.
guns.quote: I would also break with Democrats to protect the Second Amendment and the right of law-abiding citizens to own firearms.

energy.text: He supports clean energy sources and innovation while saying energy should remain affordable and opposing mandates that burden consumers.
energy.quote: I support an all-of-the-above energy strategy that includes wind, hydroelectric, solar, and other emerging technologies while ensuring energy remains affordable for working families.

tax.text: He voted for H.R. 1 and said it would prevent a tax hike on Michigan families.
tax.quote: This bill delivers on our promises to the American people to prevent a tax hike that would cost them thousands

wages.text: He voted against the 2019 Raise the Wage Act, which proposed increasing the federal minimum wage.
wages.quote:
Vote Question: On Passage
Raise the Wage Act
Vote Type: Recorded Vote
Status: Passed

trade.text: He backed tariffs on Chinese imports and introduced legislation to revoke China’s permanent normal trade relations status.
trade.quote: President Trump’s recent tariffs and the Restoring Trade Fairness Act, which I introduced earlier this year to revoke China's permanent normal trade relations status, will finally put an end to this abuse—holding China accountable and protecting American jobs.

debt.text: He says changes to Social Security and Medicare should be grandfathered so they do not reduce benefits for retirees or people nearing retirement.
debt.quote: any changes to these programs must be grandfathered in so they do not affect the benefits retirees and individuals nearing retirement receive.

housing.text: He requested funding for local housing projects that he said would increase supply and improve affordability.
housing.quote: The project is a valuable use of taxpayer funds because it will increase housing supply and improve home affordability

schools.text: He said parents should be able to choose schools that fit their students’ needs and has co-chaired the Congressional School Choice Caucus.
schools.quote: I believe when parents are given the power to choose the school that fits the needs of their students, they will make the right choice.

safety.text: On opioid policy, he said communities need resources for prevention, treatment, and law enforcement.
safety.quote: The fight against the opioid crisis takes many forms and I am working on all fronts to make sure our communities have the resources they need for prevention, treatment and law enforcement.

immigration.text: He voted for H.R. 1, which he said would empower Border Patrol and ICE to secure the southern border.
immigration.quote: empower U.S. Border Patrol and ICE to secure the southern border

guns.text: He describes the right to bear arms as a fundamental principle and says it must be preserved.
guns.quote: As a supporter of the Second Amendment, I believe the right to bear arms is a fundamental principle upon which the founders built our nation.

abortion.text: He says life begins at conception and has publicly pledged to defend unborn life.
abortion.quote: I believe that everyone has an unalienable right to life and that life begins at conception.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: He voted for the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act, which addresses participation in sports by sex.
gender.quote: Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act

cannabis.text: He voted against the MORE Act, a bill to legalize marijuana federally.
cannabis.quote:
Vote Question: On Passage
MORE Act
Vote Type: Yea-And-Nay
Status: Passed

health.text: He rejects a single-payer Medicare-for-All system and favors patient and family choice in coverage and treatment.
health.quote: A single-payer, Medicare for All approach is not the answer.

energy.text: He supports an all-of-the-above energy strategy using domestic resources and says energy policy should reduce prices.
energy.quote: Our nation's long-term energy policy must be aimed at reducing prices for American families and businesses. I support an all-of-the-above energy strategy that utilizes our nation's abundant domestic resources so we can continue to be an energy-independent nation.

voting.text: He supports the SAVE America Act and said reforms are needed to prevent non-citizens from registering and voting.
voting.quote: It makes clear that reforms are needed to stop non-citizens from registering and casting a vote.

immigration.text: She says immigration-related constitutional protections should be expanded to all individuals regardless of citizenship.
immigration.quote: the only improvements that I could support are those that would increase the rights of all individuals regardless of citizenship.

health.text: She says she fully supports a single-payer system covering preventive and urgent care, prescriptions, mental health, dental, and eye care.
health.quote: I 100% support a single payer system for all preventative and urgent care needs including prescriptions, mental health, dental, and eye care.
